definition: Forcing model output to conform to a schema, via instructions, function-calling formats, or grammar-constrained decoding.
details: Forcing model output to conform to a schema, via instructions, function-calling formats, or grammar-constrained decoding. The difference between a demo and a system: downstream code needs guaranteed parseability.

explainer.lead: Forcing model output to conform to a schema, via instructions, function-calling formats, or grammar-constrained decoding. It matters because it is the difference between a demo and a system: downstream code needs guaranteed parseability.

tiers.eli5: It's like giving a form to fill in instead of a blank page, so the next program can read the answers every time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers constrain responses with instructions, function-calling formats or grammar-constrained decoding so downstream code can parse them; the pitfall is assuming free-form generations will always parse.
tiers.paperLevel: Output is constrained to a schema through instructions, function-calling formats, or grammar-constrained decoding; the requirement is guaranteed parseability for downstream code.

explainer.example: A model asked for a JSON object returns one matching the given schema so a program can consume it directly.
